why: .env-production (dash) and Wrangler's .dev.vars are dotenv files under other names; cat'ing them must hide quoted secrets
Spring Boot's application.properties uses lowercase dotted names (spring.datasource.password=...); the credential-name rule must apply in this convention too, not only to UPPER_SNAKE

`cat ${HOME}/.my.cnf` names a home credential file, but namedSecretFiles only expands ~/ and $HOME/, so the output isn't masked; my.cnf's lowercase `password=` then escapes the uppercase-only NAME=value pattern
a hard-coded SECRET_KEY and DATABASES password in settings.py use Python's `NAME = 'value'` and `'PASSWORD': 'value'` forms; the agent reads settings.py all the time
`wg showconf` prints INI with `Key = value`; PrivateKey and PresharedKey are secret, PublicKey and AllowedIPs are what the agent debugs

why: `grep ^DB_PASSWORD= .env | cut -d= -f2` names .env, but prints only the bare value: masking has no name to go on and a word-like password isn't registered
docker inspect of another project's container: the NAME=value pattern stops at a comma or space, so a password containing one is masked only up to that character
`od -A x -t x1z` is the POSIX sibling of hexdump -C: its 6-digit offsets don't match the hex-dump decoder (7-8 digits), so the hex column still spells out the secret 16 bytes at a time
secrets.staging.yml / secrets.prod.json are secret files just like secrets.yml; under them a 32-hex admin key with a neutral name is only hidden by secret-file masking

the `name: value` pattern's `:\s+` crosses the newline after a parent key (`datasource:`), so the parent swallows its first child line and a password that is the first key under its parent is never checked
